title: The bait mode's first wave: Reeds of 20 hp hunt Isao before the boss, held to a solver budget, with an fps corner
context: Owner, 2026-10-09: "let's test something with the fps; wave 1 is 5 to 50 (slider) Reed - four limbs, creatures, smaller (size 15) and with only 20 hp, not 180. once they are defeated, the bigger Nih Dairia shows up." The kit's soft body steps at 240 Hz; the question was what N of them cost. Bait mode only; the tank mode and the wave-less flow (count 0) unchanged; src/fx/nih-dairia untouched.
outcome: PHASE 1, MEASURED FIRST (scratch probe, headless Chrome, the lab's scene, the kit's factory and wasm kernel, each Reed's update(dt) as the lab steps the boss; frame ms is the rAF interval, vsync-bound at 16.7): boss alone (1,187 nodes) solver 4.2 ms mean / 5.1 p95 a frame (1.05 ms a step), skin 0.19, 126 draw calls, frame 16.7; nothing stepped: 64 draws; 1 Reed (877 nodes, 2,382 tets): solver 3.2 / 4.0, skin 0.18, frame 16.7 / 18.5, 126 draws, heap 156 MB; 5 Reeds: 12.1 / 14.6, skin 0.67, frame 16.7, 135 draws, 168 MB; 10 Reeds: 70.9 / 72.4 ms, skin 1.4, frame 73 ms (the kit's fixed stepper caught up 12 steps a Reed a frame: a spiral), 148 draws; 20: 139 / 145, frame 141; 50: 359 / 362, skin 6.7, frame 354 ms (under 3 fps), 213 draws, heap 346 MB; the boss in the bait seat with 50 Reeds: 375 ms, 351 draws. A Reed step costs about 0.6 ms, so one Reed at real time is ~145 ms of solver a second: about six fit a frame at 60 fps. Each createNihDairia without a `cage` fetched and parsed the variant's model (9-34 ms each). Solver variants on 10 Reeds over 6 sim-seconds: iterations 2 cut a sim-second from 145 to 116 ms, iterations 1 to 90, a 1/120 s step to 79 (73 with iterations 2), all finite and walking ~10.6 m/s; none adopted (the kit's feel is the owner's; noted as levers). BUILD: src/domain/boss-wave.js (makeWave, wavePlaces, resolveReeds with the fight's splashDamage on each Reed's nearest contact and streams by dt, hurtReed, waveCleared, bossEnters once, nearestReed by contacts, entryClear) with test/boss-wave.mjs; BOSS_FIGHT.wave { count 10, reedHealth 20, size 15, inset 15, corpse 2, clear 45, budget 10, lod false }. src/labs/boss/wave.js: the Reeds simulate in the lab's frame plane (native = local / scale) like the boss, so the routing, the clamp and the re-anchor's shift are the lab's (`shiftKit`, `kitNow`, `nodesOf` moved into body.js and shared); each Reed is drawn through its own frame on the sphere under its centre (a flat floor 105 m out floats 7 m over the sphere). The model is parsed once (`loadMonsterCage`) and each Reed gets a copy with its own surface geometry and the bindings shared: heap at 50 Reeds 153-169 MB against 346. Each Reed has its own fear (createFear, the per-gun fear) and temperament (lunges seeded apart); its target is Isao's ground point through arena.route and arena.clamp (or its flee point). Every player round resolves on every live Reed (the seat's resolve calls the friendlies' and the wave's; the boss held back takes nothing). The dead collapse (motion off, gravity 10) and are disposed after 2 s. While the wave holds, the boss is hidden and unstepped (its fear and temperament off, no re-anchor), and the rules' creature for Isao's autopilot, his hold (LOST Isao taken), his lines, the seat's focus and ISAO · CAM is the Reed nearest him by its floor contacts. The last Reed dead, the boss enters at the arena's centre and Isao is put out to 45 m if nearer. The bar reads WAVE 1 · REED n/N; R restarts the wave; ?reeds=N and the panel's `wave 1 (bait)` folder (0-50, Reed health, the budget, the off-screen half rate). THE BUDGET: the frame's need is priced from the running cost of a step and past `budget` ms the whole wave's clock slows alike (no catch-up spiral). The fps corner (top left, shown in the friends' link too) reads fps, solver ms, Reeds and the wave's clock. AFTER THE BUILD (--boss-wave, headless): 10 Reeds 48.7-50 fps, solver 9.9-10.0 ms, the wave's clock x0.28-0.32 (a step now 0.76 ms with the fear and the temperament); 50 Reeds 42-45 fps, solver 9.9-10.1 ms, clock x0.044-0.048. The off-screen half rate bought 0.053 and 0.068 against 0.048 and 0.044 (13 and 27 of 50 off-screen) and no fps; at 10 Reeds none or two are off-screen: kept as a knob, off. No obstacle push-out for the Reeds (they route round the rocks; the bound clamps their targets).
alternatives: Each Reed in its own re-anchored surface frame (rejected: the rules would need every contact converted between frames; drawing through a per-Reed frame over the shared plane gives the same picture with the lab's rules untouched)
Each Reed at most one kernel step a frame (the brief's example; subsumed: a time budget across the wave, which is the same at its tight end and lets a small wave run at full rate)
A coarser step or fewer iterations for the Reeds (measured: 1/120 s halves the cost; left to the owner, it changes the kit's feel)
The off-screen half rate on by default (measured too small a gain; a knob)
evidence: node --check on every edited file; npm test (225 programs, boss-wave.mjs new), npm run check, npm run build green

from an APFS snapshot, sequentially, one headless Chrome (memory WARN on swap): --boss-wave (twice green), --boss-friends, --boss-bait (with boss-bait-friends; it and --boss-under load ?reeds=0, the copy block's ninth line is the wave), --boss green

--boss-wave: ten Reeds 105 m out, the bar WAVE 1 · REED 10/10, the boss hidden; in 8 s of lab clock their mean distance to Isao fell 108.9-109.1 to 90.8-92.5 m; scripted fire killed 2 with the 40 mm and 1 with the 25 mm (Isao 12/12); killReeds() the rest: the boss at 0.1 m from the centre, shown, stepping, its bar 180/180, Isao 45 m out when he was put; R: ten again, the boss held back; 50 Reeds all loaded
